newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto unit recalls some insect spray.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto unit recalls some insect spray.

text.p: The Solaris Group, a unit of Monsanto Co, said on Thursday it has issued a voluntary limited recall of an insect spray sold under the name Ortho Diazinon Plus.
The insecticide is mixed with water and used outdoors to control bugs on flowers, shrubs, fruits, vegetables and lawns.

The recalled units come in one-pint plastic containers and carry the lot codes A31246M, A21276M and A31276M. They lack an emulsifier that enables the insecticide to mix thoroughly with water, the company said.
If the defective insecticide is sprayed on plants, it may not work, the company said.
If fruits or vegetables that have been sprayed are eaten, the person may suffer headaches and nausea because the concentration of insecticide might be above federal limits, Monsanto said.
The ommission of the emulsifier was blamed on human error.

The problem was limited to only one production run, which a Monsanto spokeswoman called "relatively minor." She said less than 4,000 units of the product were affected, and the company has already recovered about one-third of that amount from distributors.
